Hip-hop's family tree starts at a Kingston street dance 🇯🇲 Save this, then grab a mic:

🔊 Sound systems (crews of disc jockeys, engineers and MCs) got popular in Kingston in the 1950s
🔊 Early sound men like Tom the Great Sabastian mixed American R&B, soul and jazz with mento and ska
🔊 Jamaica's culture minister Olivia Grange calls the sound system the "base and root" of Jamaican music
🔊 Aug 11, 1973: Jamaican-born DJ Kool Herc's back-to-school jam in the West Bronx, promoted by his sister Cindy
🔊 The DJ-and-MC pairing at hip-hop's core descends from Jamaican toasting and sound clash culture
🔊 Grandmaster Flash immigrated from Barbados

🎤 The DJ and the mic are in Brooklyn tonight: Dancehall Meets R&B Karaoke Pt 2 with DJ BigReef and DJ Trixta, hosted by Ace General · 333 Lounge & Restaurant, 333 Flatbush Ave, Prospect Heights · on till 1 AM

Sources: Jamaica Information Service, TIME

items.caption:
Four kinds of roti, and you've probably only ordered one 🫓 Save this for your next roti run:

🫓 Indentured workers brought roti from India to Trinidad in the 1800s
🫓 Over the next century it took on East Indian, West African, Spanish, French and other influences from Trinidad's kitchens
🫓 Trinidad grew its own styles: dhalpuri, sada, dosti and buss up shut (paratha)
🫓 Dhalpuri hides ground split peas inside the dough
🫓 Buss up shut gets busted apart on the stove into soft shreds, made for dipping in curry
🫓 The Trini wrap turned roti into "a meal all its own", folded around curried chicken, potato or pumpkin

📍 Where to order in NYC:
· Trinciti Roti Shop @trinciti_ny · 111-03 Lefferts Blvd, South Ozone Park, Queens · dhalpuri roti, doubles and bake n shark · family-owned since 2005 · closed Mondays
· Melanie's Roti & Grill · 1248 Castle Hill Ave, the Bronx · Guyanese: dhal puri, pholourie and goat curry

Sources: The World, Oxford Business Group; shop details from trinciti.nyc and melaniesrotigrillrestaurant.com

alt: Cover: Culture. Know your roti. Four styles, and where to order one. Save this before your next roti run.

India to Trinidad: indentured workers brought roti from India to Trinidad in the 1800s; over the next century it took on East Indian, West African, Spanish, French and other influences; the Trini wrap made it a meal all its own, folded around curried chicken, potato or pumpkin.

The styles: dhalpuri has ground split peas hidden inside the dough; buss up shut, or paratha, is busted apart on the stove into soft shreds for dipping in curry; sada and dosti are two more styles Trinidad grew. Sources: The World, Oxford Business Group.

Where to order in NYC: Trinciti Roti Shop, 111-03 Lefferts Boulevard, South Ozone Park, Queens, with dhalpuri roti, doubles and bake n shark, closed Mondays; Melanie's Roti and Grill, 1248 Castle Hill Avenue, the Bronx, Guyanese, with dhal puri, pholourie and goat curry.

items.caption:
Sorrel needs two to three days to steep. Start by Monday and it's ready for Thanksgiving 🌺

Every Caribbean auntie knows the red drink doesn't happen overnight. The classic method:

1️⃣ Boil it with ginger and spices
2️⃣ Steep it for two to three days
3️⃣ Add sugar, wine or rum

And the story in the cup:
🌺 Sorrel is brewed from roselle, a tropical hibiscus. It's the same plant behind bissap in many African countries
🌺 Food historians tie it to red drinks that crossed the Atlantic during the slave trade. In Jamaica, it became sorrel
🌺 It's a Christmas drink for a practical reason: the plant was historically only available around Christmastime
🌺 The same hibiscus pours as agua de Jamaica in Latinx kitchens
🌺 Caribbean immigrants carried sorrel to US cities starting in the 1930s

Sources: WLRN
